state:
**Goal `tooling-overhaul`: Stages 9 and 10 are done, and Stage 11 is in progress.** The cutover is on `main`. `main` stays frozen, and tag `pre-overhaul` is the rollback.

Both Stage 11 checks pass. `bun nv audit ci` prints both of its `want` lines. `bun nv loop-stats` (`tools/nv/cmd/loop-stats.ts`) is the port of `tools/loop-stats.py`, with every report: the default one (per session, constants, head, drift, projection, group curve), `--attribute`, `--calibrate [--write]` and `--json`. It adds `--guard`: the guard's denials per rule and per session, read from `hook error: guard: <rule>:` tool results. A rule is flagged `RISING` when the later half of the sessions since its first denial counts more than the earlier half. The port also recognises `bun nv peek`, `nv orient` and `data/goals/`, which the Python tool misses. So its attribution differs from the Python tool's by a few percent, and its constants match exactly.

`tools/loop-stats.py` is still on disk, and so are its citations (`AGENTS.md`, `docs/agent/*.md`). The same holds for every other Python tool ported so far. Deleting them and repointing the citations is Stage 12's work (`no Python`). `tool("loop-stats")` in `tools/nv/cmd/orient.ts` already resolves to `bun nv loop-stats`, because the command file exists.
